annotations.keyFindings: A pre-assessment dose-adjustment plan was followed by fewer out-of-range day-of-surgery values (34 to 21 percent) and fewer infusions (46 to 18 percent).
annotations.notes: Closest to the protocol's first component.

annotations.keyFindings: A pilot trial of a pre-surgery nurse call recruited 48 percent of eligible patients but had only 79 percent outcome completeness.
First-on-the-list scheduling was achievable for most general surgery and urology patients and shortened fasting by about three hours.
annotations.notes: Supports the scheduling component across specialties.

annotations.keyFindings: Correction scales were associated with less hypoglycaemia than infusions for short operations (4 against 9 percent).

claims.text: A pre-assessment dose-adjustment plan was followed by fewer patients with out-of-range glucose on the day of surgery.
claims.interpretation: Planning value for the primary outcome.

claims.text: First-on-the-list scheduling was achieved for most general surgery and urology patients.

synthesis: Four retrieved records appraised at abstract level: a dose-adjustment plan, a nurse call pilot, scheduling feasibility and correction scales each have supportive observational or pilot evidence.
summary: Retrieved records appraised; two claims recorded; certainty low.
